extracted.intended_audience: government contracting officers, contract administrators, and contractors (procurement/procurement quality assurance)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and standards for government contracting cost allowability, property/tooling disposition, procurement quality assurance (including selective evaluation), and compensation/benefit-related cost principles for contractors performing Federal contracts. Covers procedures that contracting officers and contractors must follow and criteria for judging reasonableness and allowability of costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective evaluation at the subcontract level
rubrics_metrics.description: Selective evaluation of the contractor’s control of his subcontractors may be requested by the contract administration office responsible for the contract in order to provide that office with additional assurance that supplies and services being received from subcontractors conform to quality requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications between contract administration offices concerning procurement quality assurance actions to be performed shall be through Government channels. Requests for selective evaluation shall indicate Government procurement quality actions to be performed, e.g., specific characteristics, processes and procedures to be verified, tests to be witnessed, and records, reports, and certificates to be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of special tooling (Contracting Officer actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When production ceases for designated products/parts/services, the Contracting Officer shall, within ninety days after receipt of any list or notice, furnish to the Contractor a list specifying products/parts/services for which the Government may require special tooling along with a request that the Contractor transfer title and deliver all usable special tooling used or designed for the manufacture or performance of such designated portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Contracting Officer must (i) specify items, (ii) accept or reject offers by the Contractor under paragraph (e), (iii) direct the Contractor to sell or dispose of items as scrap for the Government's account, (iv) state waiver of Government interest in tooling, or (v) any combination as warranted. Failure to give directions within the period is construed as direction to sell/dispose under (iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of special tooling (Contractor duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request of the Contracting Officer to transfer title or deliver special tooling, the Contractor shall promptly comply and either (1) prepare items for shipment by proper packaging, packing, and marking and promptly deliver as directed, or (2) prepare items for storage in accordance with a storage agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent compliance occasions any uncompensated cost to the Contractor, the contract price shall be equitably adjusted per the Changes clause. Items delivered or stored shall be accompanied by operation sheets or other appropriate data necessary to show manufacturing operations/processes. If further negotiations are requested by the Contracting Officer, the Contractor shall negotiate in good faith. Items not disposed of by transfer or acceptance of offers shall be disposed of as directed (sell/scrap or waive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of cost reasonableness (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost is reasonable if, in its nature or amount, it does not exceed that which would be incurred by an ordinarily prudent person in the conduct of competitive business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining reasonableness consider: (1) whether the cost is generally recognized as ordinary and necessary for the contractor’s business or contract performance; (2) restraints/requirements imposed by accepted business practices, arm’s-length bargaining, Federal/State laws/regulations, and contract terms/specifications; (3) what a prudent business person would do considering responsibilities to owners, employees, customers, Government, and the public; and (4) significant deviations from established contractor practices which may unjustifiably increase contract costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CWAS application and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where allowability of an indirect cost is based on reasonableness, reasonableness may be determined by reliance on the contractor weighted average share in cost risk (CWAS) computed from data of the year the cost was incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the profit center has a CWAS rating of 65 points or higher, with at least 35 points derived from competitive firm fixed-price contracts and commercial sales, the reasonableness of the cost will not be questioned. If CWAS is 50–64, application of the subdivision may be at the discretion of the administrative contracting officer. Sections subject to CWAS are indicated by (CWAS) and those not applicable by (CWAS-NA). If cost reasonableness is not determined under CWAS because of inapplicability, determination is made per the general reasonableness paragraph. If contractor cannot or does not choose to qualify under CWAS, determine per the general paragraph. Corporate CWAS should be used for corporate-type expenses allocated to profit centers; intermediate management organizations should develop CWAS ratings; certain indirect costs applied to specific contracts may be excluded from CWAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation for personal services — scope and basic allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation for personal services includes all remuneration paid or accrued for services rendered by employees during contract performance and is allowable if reasonable and not in excess of costs allowable by the Internal Revenue Code and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes salaries, directors' and executive committee members' fees, bonuses (including incentive awards), options, benefits, and contributions to pension/annuity/management incentive plans. Allowability requires that total compensation for individual employees be reasonable for services rendered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for compensation reasonableness (CWAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation is reasonable to the extent that the total amount paid or accrued is commensurate with the contractor's established policy and conforms generally to compensation paid by other firms of the same size, in the same industry, or geographic area for similar services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every compensation case need be subjected to detailed testing; detailed tests apply when a general review reveals amounts or types appearing unreasonable or out of line. Special conditions may require limitation, including: (i) compensation to owners/close family members or those acquiring substantial financial interest — must be for actual services not profit distribution (CWAS-NA); (ii) changes in compensation policy causing substantial increases concurrent with increased ratio of Government contracts (CWAS); (iii) contractor business not subject to normal competitive restraints (CWAS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation in lieu of salary for partners and sole proprietors
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation in lieu of salary for services rendered by partners and sole proprietors will be allowed to the extent that it is reasonable and does not constitute a distribution of profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (CWAS) Apply reasonableness test and ensure amounts are for services, not profit distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor-management agreement costs limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of compensation resulting from provisions of labor-management agreements are not allowable to the extent they are determined to be unreasonable because unwarranted by the character/circumstances of the work or discriminatory against the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application of such provisions to Government contracts may be unwarranted when circumstances differ (e.g., less hazardous work or continual overtime). Disallowance under this subparagraph will not be made unless (i) the contractor has been permitted opportunity to justify the costs, and (ii) due consideration has been given to whether unusual conditions pertain to the Government contract work imposing burdens/hardships/hazards requiring higher compensation to attract/retain personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Salaries and wages for current services include gross compensation paid to employees in cash, products, or services, and are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (CWAS) Allowable as current service compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash bonuses and incentive compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Incentive compensation for management employees, cash bonuses, safety awards, and incentive compensation based on production/cost reduction/efficient performance are allowable to the extent overall compensation is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such costs must be paid or accrued pursuant to an agreement entered into in good faith between the contractor and the employees before the services were rendered, or pursuant to an established plan consistently followed by the contractor implying an agreement to make such payments. Deferred bonuses and incentive compensation are subject to deferred compensation rules (paragraph (f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonuses and incentive compensation paid in stock
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of bonuses and incentive compensation paid in the stock of the contractor or an affiliate are allowable subject to the same rules as cash bonuses, with additional requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requirements: (1) valuation placed on stock transferred shall be fair market value at time of transfer determined on the most objective basis available; (2) accruals for stock cost prior to issuance are subject to adjustment according to the possibility employees will not receive such stock and forfeiture possibilities. Such costs are subject to adjustment per deferred compensation principles and §15.107.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock options
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of options to employees to purchase stock of the contractor or an affiliate is unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (CWAS-NA) Explicitly disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred compensation — definition and allowability tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferred compensation includes remuneration not paid until after a stated period or occurrence of events (excluding normal accounting period accruals), including pension, annuity, stock bonus, profit sharing, disability, withdrawal, insurance, survivorship, and other deferred compensation whether paid in cash or stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferred compensation is allowable to the extent that: (i) except for past service pension/retirement costs, it is for services rendered during the contract period; (ii) it is reasonable in amount together with all other compensation paid; (iii) it is paid pursuant to an agreement entered into in good faith before services were rendered or pursuant to an established, consistently followed plan; and (iv) for plans subject to IRS approval, it falls within criteria and standards of the Internal Revenue Code and IRS regulations. See §15.107 for related limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred compensation — adjustments for forfeitures and abnormal forfeitures
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate adjustments shall be made for credits or gains (including those from normal and abnormal employee turnover) or other contingencies resulting in forfeiture of deferred compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments only for forfeitures that inure to contractor benefit; forfeitures benefiting other employees without reducing contractor costs normally don't give rise to adjustment. Adjustments for normal turnover based on contractor experience and foreseeable prospects. Rules for abnormal forfeitures: (i) foreseeable abnormal forfeitures that can be evaluated with reasonable accuracy (actuarial or other sound computation) shall be reflected by adjustment of current costs; (ii) abnormal forfeitures not within (i) may be made the subject of agreement between Government and contractor as to equitable adjustment or method of determining such adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred compensation — future vs. contract-period services
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether deferred compensation is for services rendered during the contract period or for future services, consider conditions imposed on eventual payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider requirements such as continued consultation after retirement and covenants not to compete when deciding whether deferred compensation relates to services during the contract period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefits are allowances and services provided by the contractor to employees as compensation in addition to regular wages and salaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (CWAS) Costs of fringe benefits (vacations, holidays, sick leave, military leave, employee insurance, supplemental unemployment benefit plans) are allowable to the extent required by law, employer-employee agreement, or an established policy of the contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and repair costs — normal vs extraordinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs necessary for the upkeep of property (including Government property unless otherwise provided) which neither add to the permanent value nor appreciably prolong its intended life but keep it in an efficient operating condition are treated as maintenance/repair costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (CWAS) Normal maintenance and repair costs are allowable. Extraordinary maintenance and repair costs are allowable provided such are allocated to the periods to which applicable for purposes of determining contract costs (see §15.107).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant and equipment expenditures (capitalization/depreciation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenditures for plant and equipment, including rehabilitation, which according to generally accepted accounting principles as applied under the contractor’s established policy should be capitalized and subjected to depreciation, are allowable only on a depreciation basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (CWAS-NA) Capital expenditures must be treated per GAAP and recovered through depreciation rather than current expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation costs — allowability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Relocation costs (of specified covered types) are allowable subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (CWAS) Conditions: (1) the move is for the benefit of the employer; (2) reimbursement is in accordance with an established policy or practice consistently followed by the employer designed to motivate employees to relocate promptly and economically; (3) the costs are not otherwise unallowable under §15.205-33 or other sections (see §15.107 regarding large scale relocation); and (4) amounts reimbursed shall not exceed the employee’s actual (or reasonably estimated) expenses.
